extra.message: CSRF via GET-based account enable/disable toggle — Cross-site request can force a school admin session to disable or re-enable arbitrary user accounts, including causing account lockout [verified: admin_user_toggle is GET-routed and toggles account active state with no method check, enabling forced account lockout via CSRF.]

Unvalidated role field and hardcoded weak default password in admin CSV import — A malicious or malformed CSV row can create accounts with an invalid/unexpected role value, and any imported account without an explicit password gets a well-known, hardcoded default password that could be used to log in before the user resets it. [verified: role=row.get('role','student') is passed straight into create_user with no allowlist check, and ROLE_CHOICES includes 'school_admin', so a CSV row can create a privileged account; missing password also defaults to hardcoded 'changeme123'.]

IDOR on resource file download when resource has no course or requester is a TA — Any authenticated user (student, TA, or otherwise unrelated user) can download arbitrary course/lesson resource files by iterating pk values, exposing potentially restricted course materials, datasets, or other uploaded files outside their enrollment/teaching scope. [verified: When resource.course is None (nullable field), the entire access-check block at views.py:859-863 is skipped and any authenticated user's request reaches FileResponse; TAs are also never checked when course is set.]

Unauthenticated disclosure of sensitive course operational data — Any unauthenticated network client can retrieve sensitive internal course financial/renewal and owner-contact metadata without any credentials, unlike every other endpoint in the same module which requires an internal token. [verified: course_grade_file_096 at line 50 lacks the `_wrk_gate` check present in every sibling endpoint, allowing any unauthenticated request to retrieve sensitive ops_memo data (renewal risk, payment flags, owner contact details).]

Plaintext storage and weak generation of API keys and webhook secrets — Compromise of the database or admin panel directly yields usable, long-lived API keys and webhook secrets without needing to crack a hash. [verified: ApiKey.key and Webhook.secret are plaintext CharFields (core/models.py:367-390), directly exposed via admin.site.register with default ModelAdmin (core/admin.py:76-77), so any admin/DB access discloses usable long-lived credentials.]

CSRF via state-changing GET endpoints — Cross-site request forgery can disable/enable accounts, moderate discussions, release grades, or request resubmissions on behalf of a logged-in victim without their consent [verified: discussion_moderate, admin_user_toggle, release_grade, request_resubmission, and assignment_status are GET-routed (core/urls.py) with only @login_required/@is_school_admin author checks and no require_POST/require_http_methods guard, and Django's CSRF middleware does not cover GET, so these state changes are forgeable cross-site against a logged-in victim.]

CSRF via GET-based grade release — Cross-site request can force an instructor/admin session to release a grade to a student prematurely [verified: release_grade is GET-routed and mutates grade/submission state with no method check.]

CSRF via GET-based resubmission request — Cross-site request can force instructor/TA session to flag a student's submission as needing resubmission [verified: request_resubmission is GET-routed and mutates submission.status with no method check.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — If deployed with SECRET_KEY unset, sessions, password-reset tokens, and other signed data can be forged since the fallback value is predictable/public. [verified: settings.py:9 falls back to a fixed, guessable SECRET_KEY with no startup check enforcing an env override, so a misconfigured deployment forges signed sessions/tokens.]

Hardcoded default SECRET_KEY and DB credentials fallback — Session/CSRF/password-reset token forgery via known SECRET_KEY if deployed without overriding env vars; DB compromise via default lms_pass credentials [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback plus DATABASE_URL default credentials in settings.py; both are silent fallbacks rather than hard failures, so a deploy without env overrides runs with known secrets.]

Missing thread-scope validation on discussion comment replies — Cross-thread comment association bypassing thread-level moderation/visibility boundaries; can be used to leak the existence of comments across threads a user shouldn't be able to correlate. [verified: parent_id is resolved via get_object_or_404(DiscussionComment, pk=parent_id) with no check that comment.thread==thread, allowing cross-thread parent linkage; impact is limited to comment association/visibility leakage, not data exposure of restricted content.]

CSRF via GET-based discussion moderation — Cross-site request can force instructor/TA/admin session to hide/lock/pin a discussion thread [verified: discussion_moderate is GET-routed and mutates thread.status with no method check.]
